name: North Bend
seo_title: 4 Christmas Events for Kids in North Bend, WA 2026
seo_desc: 4 Christmas events for kids in North Bend, WA, 1 free: Holly Days Winter Festival and Tree Lighting and Santa Breakfast at Mt. Si Senior Center and more.
lede: North Bend celebrates in the shadow of Mount Si with a downtown Holly Days festival and tree lighting, plus a Santa breakfast and holiday events at local venues.
celebrates: North Bend's big night is Holly Days, an annual winter festival and tree lighting organized by the North Bend Downtown Foundation with the City of North Bend. It features fireside s'mores, hot cocoa, holiday crafts, live local entertainment and photos with Santa, and Mayor Mary Miller leads the tree lighting. A free showing of the movie Elf at the North Bend Theatre comes earlier in the day. The same day, the Mt. Si Senior Center serves a Santa Breakfast that raises money for its programs, and later in December a retreat center and a holiday gala for foster and kinship youth add more family choices.
lastyear: In 2025 the Mt. Si Senior Center held its Santa Breakfast on Saturday, December 6, from 8:30 to 11 am, with warm pancakes, a visit with Santa and time together, as the center described it on its own site. The North Bend Downtown Foundation also ran the downtown holiday lighting program under its agreement with the city, which calls for 36 Christmas poles with lit garland, 26 winter trees with warm lights and lighting of the train depot building.
facts: North Bend's townsite was platted in 1889 by William H. Taylor when he learned that a Seattle railroad wanted a station on his farmland. It was first called Snoqualmie, then Mountain View, and finally North Bend. Mount Si, the peak above town, is named for Josiah Merritt, known as Uncle Si, who arrived in 1862. Logging powered the economy, with a lumbering boom in 1908 when two sawmills operated, and North Bend incorporated in 1909. Motorists headed to Snoqualmie Pass first used the Sunset Highway and today use Interstate 90.
trains: North Bend's town history starts with the railroad, because Taylor platted the townsite in 1889 when a Seattle railroad wanted a station on his land, and the city still lights the train depot building for the holidays. There is no Sounder, Link or Amtrak stop in North Bend, and the nearest hub for those trains is King Street Station in Seattle, about 30 miles west. For a holiday train ride, the Northwest Railway Museum in nearby Snoqualmie runs historic trains, and the Seattle Center Monorail is a short ride in Seattle.

faq: How does North Bend celebrate Christmas?

The North Bend Downtown Foundation hosts Holly Days, a winter festival and tree lighting with s'mores, hot cocoa, crafts, live music and Santa photos. The Mt. Si Senior Center also holds a Santa Breakfast, and the downtown depot, poles and trees are lit for the season.
Where is the North Bend tree lighting?

In 2026 it moves to East North Bend Way, where a living tree next to Rio Bravo restaurant is the Community Tree. Part of E McClellan Street and the park and ride are closed for the event, so check the city's parking page.

Yes. The city's calendar lists Holly Days as free, and the organizers describe it as a free event supported by donations from local businesses. Some extras, such as food at nearby restaurants, are not part of the festival, so bring a little spending money if you want a treat.
Can kids ride a Christmas train near North Bend?

The Northwest Railway Museum in neighboring Snoqualmie runs historic trains and holiday rides. Check the museum's own Santa Trains page for dates, times and prices, since the museum sets them. The depot is a short drive west of North Bend in Historic Downtown Snoqualmie, near Railroad Park, and families often pair a train ride with a stop at the shops along Railroad Avenue.
Where does North Bend's name come from?

The townsite was first named Snoqualmie, then Mountain View. The railroad asked William Taylor, who platted the town in 1889, to change the name because another town just four miles away was called Snoqualmie Falls, so it finally became North Bend, the name that stuck.
